title: Surjective pointed map from the neighbourhood colimit to the relative separable closure
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $y$ its image. Give $\Omega$ its $\kappa(y)$-algebra structure [def-weil-residue-field] via the residue embedding of $\bar y$. Write $K=\kappa(y)^{\mathrm{sep}}\subset\Omega$ for the relative separable closure [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] and $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ for the chosen coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For any local-ring structure on $C$, there exists a surjective ring map $\psi:C\to K$ with kernel the maximal ideal, such that for every chosen representative affine pointed neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$, the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}(K\hookrightarrow\Omega)\circ\operatorname{Spec}\psi}\operatorname{Spec}C\xrightarrow{c_V}V$ equals $\bar v$. No residue-field equivalence, uniqueness, structural-map equation, or strict henselianity is part of this statement.

proof.text: Choose an affine chart through barY. Identify the chart residue field and its relative separable closure with those of Y through their embeddings into Ω, using hΩ. Evaluation followed by the pointed residue embedding gives a compatible residue cocone on the affine neighbourhood diagram; residue extensions are finite separable. The neighbourhood/triple comparison identifies this cocone with the triple residue cocone.

Use the coprojection equation of strictHenselization_triples to identify the cocone-induced colimit map with its specific triple residue map. Transport this map through the colimit comparison and the embedding-compatible closure identification. The triple theorem proves surjectivity for this same map; IsLocalRing.ker_eq_maximalIdeal identifies its kernel for the given local-ring instance. The abstract existential core alone cannot give properties of this specific map.

Apply Spec to the coprojection equations and the affine-scheme isomorphisms to obtain the pointed factorization over the chart. Any neighbourhood admits an affine pointed refinement over the chart. Cone naturality and pointed transition compatibility extend the equation to every SmallModel representative. This direct compatible-cocone argument remains the named hole strictHenselizationPointedMap; no universal-factorization theorem is used.
